Application Materials.content:
As part of your online application you will need to upload scanned documents. All academic documentation should be scans of the originals, not photographs. The scans should be complete and of a good quality, showing the 4 corners of all pages of the original document. Please do not merge separate qualifications together. Please do not upload academic documents to the funding section as we cannot access these.
Your application must include the following:
- A copy of your degree certificate and complete transcript. If you are still studying, please provide your latest transcript plus a list of modules yet to be studied.
- Evidence of your final or current overall % or GPA.
- A copy of your grading scale/scheme if this is not on your degree transcript.
- CV/Resume: an up-to-date CV showing your relevant work experience and education.
- CAS, BRP and Visa, for international students that have previously studied in the UK on a student visa.
- If you entered your current degree programme later than year 1, separate details of the qualification used to gain entry into that later year of your degree, including any transcripts and certificates for that qualification.
If you have them, please include the following:
- Your approved English Language test, if applicable.
- A personal statement. A personal statement is not required as standard, but could strengthen your application by explaining a gap in your education or if your education/degree subject is not directly related to the programme. The personal statement should be **no more than one side of A4** and should include details on how your prior studies are linked to your future plans and why you want to study the programme you have applied for.
Documents which are not required:
- References are not usually required, but in specific borderline cases a reference may be requested to help make a decision.
Country specific information:
- Applicants with Chinese degrees: provide evidence of your current/final overall weighted percentage (%); GPA or arithmetic percentage is not accepted.
- Applicants with Indian degrees should include: a copy of your bachelor’s degree certificate; a copy of your consolidated mark sheet; a copy of your semester mark sheets; a copy of your University marking scheme; official evidence of your current/final overall award as a percentage (%). If you have not completed your degree you should provide the bottom three items.
- Applicants with Canadian degrees: provide details of the grading system used on your transcript, including the percentage pass mark for your degree. If your degree was taught in English, include official evidence of this.
Supporting documents should always be sent via an enquiry or condition response in the applicant portal so the document links to the correct application automatically.

Interview Requirements.content: We aim to make decisions within **three to five weeks** if all necessary documents have been received. You will be contacted directly if we require any further information or wish to invite you for an interview or audition. You will receive an email asking you to check your applicant portal for more details.

Applicants are encouraged to apply as early as possible.

Academic Requirements.content:
A bachelor degree with a **2:1 (hons)** in a subject including, but not limited to, physical geography, environmental science, natural sciences or related discipline that can evidence quantitative and/or computing skills. Alternative subjects which may be considered include, but are not limited to, engineering, mathematics, human geography, geology, water resources engineering or management, physics, computer science or a related discipline.
All applicants should possess an interest in using data science to understand the natural environment and address environmental issues.
Applicants with a **2:2 (hons)** will be considered on a case-by-case basis where they can demonstrate relevant work experience or competence in a relevant specialist field. Professional qualifications and relevant experience can also be considered.
International applicants: The University accepts a range of [international equivalent qualifications](https://www.leeds.ac.uk/admissions-qualifications).
Applicants from China: accepted qualifications include **4 year Bachelor degrees**. The University of Leeds uses institutional lists when assessing applications from accepted Chinese institutions, and requirements may vary by school. If the course asks for **2.1**, applicants need **70%-85%, depending on your institution**. If the course asks for **2.2**, applicants need **70%-80%, depending on your institution**.

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
IELTS **6.5 overall**, with no less than **6.0 in any component**. For other English qualifications, read [English language equivalent qualifications](https://www.leeds.ac.uk/international-admissions/doc/entry-requirements "English language equivalent qualifications").
International students who do not meet the English language requirements for this programme may be able to study a postgraduate pre-sessional English course, designed with a progression route to the degree programme. Options include [Language for Science (6 weeks)](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/i204/language-for-science), [Language for Science: General Science (10 weeks)](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/i203/language-for-science-general-science), the [six week online pre-sessional](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/j615/online-academic-english-presessional-6-weeks-), the [10 week online pre-sessional](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/j614/online-academic-english-presessional-10-weeks-), and longer [postgraduate pre-sessional English courses](https://www.leeds.ac.uk/language-centre-courses/doc/masters-pre-sessional-english).

Program Overview.content:
Year of entry 2026. Start date September 2026. Delivery type: on campus. Duration: 12 Months (Full time).
The Environmental Data Science and Analytics MSc is designed to give you a fuller understanding of data and what appropriate interpretation and insight generation means in various environmental contexts. Throughout, you'll develop a broad understanding of environmental issues and how data driven analysis can help address these. You’ll build the skills needed to analyse, understand, interpret and visualise complex environmental data; generating insights that address real-world environmental challenges. You’ll apply techniques from data science including environmental modelling, machine learning, visualisation and data curation to environmental data, with a focus on analysis through programming.
At Leeds, you’ll have the opportunity to learn from leading researchers in the field, with input from the School of Geography and the School of Earth and Environment. By the end of the course, you’ll be equipped with the specialist knowledge and skills that are sought after across multiple industries, especially those dealing with large scale environmental data to address the needs of society.
The course is designed to give you an understanding of the end-to-end workflow of data in an environmental context, allowing the nuances of how and why data from the environment is collected, and the need for appropriate analysis for policy and management relevant insights. The course has a particular focus on the data science and analytic techniques, giving you the skills to apply them to complex environmental issues. A multitude of environmental data, and its specific context and form, is considered and worked with to give a breadth of experience necessary to derive insights and solutions creatively to real world problems.
You'll take compulsory modules that are designed to progressively include more programming and data science, moving from fundamental knowledge to application of skills in a creative manner. On completion of the course, you'll be able to demonstrate in-depth data science techniques to environmental data, with understanding of the data context allowing for sophisticated insight generation that is appropriate to inform decision making in multiple scenarios. The combination of relevant data science techniques to environmental data and understanding of environmental science context will allow you to demonstrate an ability to generate creative solutions, alongside insights.
Why study at Leeds:
- Globally-renowned research from the [School of Geography](https://environment.leeds.ac.uk/geography-research), [School of Earth and Environment](https://environment.leeds.ac.uk/see-research-innovation) and the [Leeds Institute for Data Analytics](https://lida.leeds.ac.uk/), the national institute for data science and artificial intelligence, feeds into the course.
- You can advance your skills and knowledge in areas such as environmental policies, programming for data science, machine learning, AI, satellite technology and interpreting large hyperdimensional data.
- You can tailor the course to suit your career aspirations with a selection of optional modules in areas like web-based GIS, GIS and environment and digital image processing for environmental remote sensing.
- You will conduct your own project work, enabling you to develop transferable skills as a researcher while investigating a real-world issue that explores and develops your interests.
- You will have access to specialist facilities including laboratories and an excellent GIS computer cluster with industry-standard software.
- Teaching is delivered by a programme team of academics actively engaged in ground-breaking research in the School of Geography and the School of Earth and Environment.
- Fieldwork opportunities allow you to develop understanding and skills in data acquisition and deployment of sensors to collect environmental data.
The project takes the place of the traditional dissertation. Your project submission is designed to reflect the types of data science outputs you might encounter in your future career in the form of a ‘notebook’-style analysis and an associated practical briefing report. This brings together skills in data science and programming, and meaningful insight generation that can be used to inform decision making in multiple contexts, including influencing policy.
The course takes a problem-based learning approach, presenting real-world problems where you must use your growing skills and knowledge to develop creative solutions. This is embodied using practical sessions, individual and group, where you’ll practice skills, reducing the number of modules that are purely lecture based. Datasets used are sourced from leading researchers in the field, or from industry, reflecting a variety of data types and contexts. A combination of face-to-face learning in practical labs, lectures, seminars, and group working is used alongside digital platforms.
You’ll be taught by an experienced team of academics and researchers who are actively engaged in cutting-edge research and part of the Centre for Spatial Analysis and Policy, River Basin Processes and Management, and Ecology and Global Change research groups within the School of Geography, School of Earth and Environment. On this course, you’ll be taught by expert academics, from lecturers through to professors. You may also be taught by industry professionals with years of experience, as well as trained postgraduate researchers.
While studying at Leeds, you’ll have the chance to work with clients and gain consultancy experience as part of a 2-week online Global Industry Programme. As a Masters student at Leeds, you’ll have the opportunity to gain real-world industry experience with the Global Industry Programme, developing key professional skills and gaining insight into working in your chosen field by helping to solve a real business problem from a live company brief. The programme is fully online and designed to fit around your studies, includes opportunities to make professional networks, and allows you to work as part of a team across disciplines to tackle real business needs.
The specific environmental context of the course allows you to enter specialised careers that require a contextual understanding of data and context from the environmental domain, including environmental consultancies, transport, engineering, utilities such as water, energy and renewables, and government agencies. More widely, the course will equip you with data science and analytical skills that are vital to many industries across the globe, including local authorities and governments, industry such as finance and telecoms, and NGOs. University of Leeds students are among the top 5 most targeted by top employers according to [The Graduate Market 2024, High Fliers Research](https://online.flippingbook.com/view/747999993/).

Curriculum.content:
Start date: September 2026. Delivery type: On campus. Duration: 12 Months (Full time).
The course is designed to give you an understanding of the end-to-end workflow of data in an environmental context, allowing the nuances of how and why data from the environment is collected, and the need for appropriate analysis for policy and management relevant insights. You'll take compulsory modules that are designed to progressively include more programming and data science, moving from fundamental knowledge to application of skills in a creative manner.
The list shown below represents typical modules/components studied and may change from time to time. [For more information and a full list of typical modules available on this course, please read Environmental Data Science and Analytics MSc in the course catalogue](https://catalogue.leeds.ac.uk/Programme/202627?code=MSC-EDS%26A-FT).
Compulsory modules:
- **Programming for Spatial Data Science - 15 credits**
- **Skills for Environmental Data Scientists - 15 credits**
- **Data to Insights in Multiple Environments - 15 credits**
- **Data Science for Practical Applications - 15 credits**
- **Creative Coding for Real World Problems - 15 credits**
- **Machine Learning for Environmental Data - 15 credits**
- **Environmental Data Science Project - 60 credits**. This project will take the place of the traditional dissertation. Your project submission is designed to reflect the types of data science outputs you might encounter in your future career in the form of a 'notebook'-style analysis and an associated practical briefing report.
Optional modules: The modules listed below are indicative of typical options.
- **GIS and Environment - 15 credits**
- **Digital Image Processing for Environmental Remote Sensing - 15 credits**
- **Environmental Assessment - 15 credits**
- **Web-Based GIS - 15 credits**
Fieldwork provides a great opportunity to study a fascinating subject in contrasting environments away from the University. On this course, we offer the opportunity to undertake fieldwork as part of the Data to Insights in Multiple Environments module, in the UK, to develop your understanding and skills in data acquisition and deployment of sensors to collect environmental data. In addition, you can also opt to conduct fieldwork as part of your dissertation.
While studying at Leeds, you'll have the chance to work with clients and gain consultancy experience as part of a 2-week online Global Industry Programme.

Cost of Attendance.content:
The information is provided as a guideline only, based on average spending. The following estimates are for a single student in 2025 based on the latest data available; actual amounts depend on accommodation type and availability, and lifestyle. They don’t include tuition fees.
| Cost item | Estimated cost per week |
| --- | --- |
| University accommodation, self-catered | £117 to £265 |
| University accommodation, catered | £205 to £273 |
| Private accommodation, self-catered | £110 to £300 (costs may be more for higher specifications) |
| Groceries: food, toiletries and cleaning products | £31 to £38 |
| Household bills: gas and/or electricity, water and broadband internet (included in most university accommodation and some private accommodation) | £14 to £17 |
| Personal costs: transport, socialising, restaurants/takeaways, clothes and mobile phone | £44 to £68 |
**Estimated total budget per week: approximately £199 to £423**

Conditional Admission Policy.content: International students who do not meet the English language requirements for this programme may be able to study the University of Leeds postgraduate pre-sessional English course to help improve their English language level. The pre-sessional course is designed with a progression route to the degree programme, with academic English taught in the context of the subject area. Relevant options include [Language for Science (6 weeks)](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/i204/language-for-science), [Language for Science: General Science (10 weeks)](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/i203/language-for-science-general-science), the [six week online pre-sessional](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/j615/online-academic-english-presessional-6-weeks-), the [10 week online pre-sessional](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/j614/online-academic-english-presessional-10-weeks-), and longer [postgraduate pre-sessional English courses](https://www.leeds.ac.uk/language-centre-courses/doc/masters-pre-sessional-english).
